entities.span: Port the already built and reviewed landing page onto the design token layer. Not a public marketing page, but a pasted link has to render as a real product.
rejected_spans: It is the front door for three audiences: the author, a few friends, and recruiters opening a link.

entities.span: **Done when:** the page renders on the real tokens at phone and desktop width;
the sign in band is reachable from the header and says plainly that accounts are not open yet
rejected_spans: rather than offering a control that leads nowhere
(feature 7 turns those into real sign in, and spec 0006 AC-7 holds this on every environment, not just production)

entities.span: the sign in band is reachable from the header and offers real sign in;
page title, description and a social preview image are set;
and crawlers are told not to index.
**The struck clause was met as written and stopped being true on 2026-08-30**, when feature 7 shipped and spec 0007 **AC-16** superseded spec 0006 **AC-7**, deleting `COPY-1` and both `soon` chips
rejected_spans: because they were false for every visitor the moment sign in worked
because a reader comparing this row against the page needs to see that the change was deliberate

entities.span: Design it (spec): `/architect entry page & link metadata` · written 2026-08-28, 17 acceptance criteria. It carries spec 0005's already deliberated composition decisions forward rather than re deciding them, settles the four that spec left open (the match bar count, the over signalled sign in band, what the sign in controls do before feature 7, and where the social preview image comes from), and corrects three untruths found in the prototype while tracing value sources.
rejected_spans: A cross check on a different model found seven unnamed values, one mis-carried decision and three soundness problems; all were verified against the files and folded in

entities.span: Build it: `/develop entry page & link metadata` · all five milestones landed.
rejected_spans: The last one to close was the thin thread, which waited on a real client rendering the link card rather than on any code

entities.span: The thin thread: the `Logo` base component, the committed Space Grotesk file and its licence, the generated `opengraph-image.tsx`, page title and description off `canonicalSiteUrl`, a header and footer shell, then a real preview deployment whose link card is confirmed to unfurl, plus the token drift guard, satisfies AC-1, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13, AC-15, AC-16
rejected_spans: **code landed 2026-08-28** on `feat/entry-page-and-link-metadata` (`4567221`), 213 unit tests green, typecheck, lint and `pnpm build` all clean, and the 1200 by 630 card was rendered and inspected locally in Space Grotesk.

**Closed 2026-08-28:** the last part, the deploy to a preview URL and the unfurl confirmation in a real client, was run by the engineer against the pull request's preview through a shareable link. The card renders in Slack and in iMessage, so AC-11 holds on the thing it actually rests on, and AC-12's `noindex` inference is settled: an unfurler is not a crawler

entities.span: The hero: a `<figure>` wrapping the one elevated `Card`, the example label, `MatchBar` at 8 of 11, the chip clusters, and every dead control rendered inert rather than linked, satisfies AC-5, AC-7, AC-9, AC-17
rejected_spans: landed 2026-08-28. Measured in the browser at 1440 pixels: exactly one elevated card on the page, the other three flat; the whole page renders five anchors and every one of them goes somewhere real, so neither provider control nor the apply control is a link. The card's numbers were checked for drift by editing the skill list and reloading, which caught two hand written copies of "8 of 11" that would not have moved with it; the score, the bar, the chips, the gap notes and the summary sentence now all derive from the one list

entities.span: The argument sections: how it works at `compact` on `sunken` with the hand copied bar collapsed onto the component, and the reasoning at `generous` on `sunken` with both comparison cards flat and identical, carrying the page's single hairline, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-3
rejected_spans: landed 2026-08-28. Measured: exactly one hairline on the whole page and it is on the reasoning section, the one boundary where the background does not change. The "most tools" bar is now a thin continuous rule rather than a second thing shaped like a `MatchBar`, AC-5

entities.span: About and the sign in band: the status card rewritten so nothing claims to work that does not, and the band stripped of its centred and narrow axes while keeping dark, satisfies AC-5, AC-6, AC-8
rejected_spans: landed 2026-08-28. The `working` list is empty of features because none has shipped, so it reads "nothing yet · this page is the first of it" rather than dropping the row, which keeps a slot for features 9, 11, 12 and 14 to move their claim into. Measured on the band: `text-align: start` and a 1152 pixel measure, the same as every other section, so dark ground is its only axis

entities.span: Compose and pass: replace the scaffold placeholder, then run the keyboard, focus, responsive and reduced motion pass at 320 and 1440 pixels and prove no client JavaScript ships, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-14
rejected_spans: landed 2026-08-28, run against the production build in a real browser. Measured rather than eyeballed: the three rhythm tiers distinct at both widths (160 / 64 / 96 pixels at 1440, 128 / 48 / 80 at 320), zero horizontal overflow at 320 with no element crossing the viewport edge, all five controls keyboard reachable in order with a 2px teal `:focus-visible` ring, the header's Sign in jumping to the band at both widths, and no `"use client"` anywhere in the page's tree. **One defect found, and it was not this feature's file:** under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the match cells still appeared one at a time, because the global override in `globals.css` zeroed `animation-duration` but left `animation-delay`. Fixed by `/debug` the same day in spec 0005's stylesheet, locked by [globals.test.ts](../../src/app/globals.test.ts), and spec 0005's verify step corrected, since it had checked the duration rather than the outcome and so passed while the bug was live

entities.span: Verify it: `/check verify entry page & link metadata` · **PASS on 2026-08-28**, all 17 acceptance criteria met against the running production build.
rejected_spans: Measured rather than eyeballed: the five section rhythms at both widths, exactly one hairline and exactly one elevated card, five anchors on the page and every one real, the band at the same alignment and measure as every other section, zero overflow at 320, all five controls keyboard reachable with the teal ring, all 20 icons hidden or named, and the 1200 by 630 card served from the route showing the mark, the headline and the amber chip. All three deliberately failing checks fired: the missing font fails the build by name, and both drift guards fail their test when a token or a rectangle moves. Three steps stay blocked, all of them the unfurl checks that need production or a protection bypass; none is an acceptance criterion. Same model wrote the code and ran this, so a fresh model `/check review` is still worth doing

entities.span: Test it: `/test entry page & link metadata` · done 2026-08-28.
rejected_spans: 77 new unit tests across 9 files plus 3 appended to [og-tokens.test.ts](../../src/features/entry-page/og-tokens.test.ts), all passing, 273 in the suite overall. Written in the `node` project with no jsdom, the same licence spec 0005 established: every module here is a stateless server component, so calling it is its behaviour. One addition to [react-element.ts](../../test/helpers/react-element.ts), `renderDeep`, which invokes a page's own section modules but STOPS at the design system, so the composed page can be asserted on the props spec 0006 is written against (`divider="hairline"`, `tone="elevated"`) rather than on class strings. The load bearing tests were checked for vacuousness rather than trusted: a second hairline, an elevated comparison card, a hand written "8 of 11" in the summary, and a provider label turned back into a link each fail the suite. That last check found a hole in the page level test itself, which was blind to a raw `<a>`; it is fixed and the mutation now fails it.
